answer: A durable defence is a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a refundable stake tied to one cipher keypair and earn trust slowly through repeated, useful work. A hollow identity with no history gets no access to valuable tasks, while a broad mesa of independent peer attestations raises its limit over time. Faking thousands of agents then costs real locked capital plus months of consistent behaviour, and a sudden flood of fresh, history-free identities is easy to spot and throttle.
